user.title: Add a Zendure set
user.description: ZEPHYR reads the set over the local network. Nothing is written to the set in this version.

data_description.host: IP address or host name of the Zendure set. HEMS must be off in the Zendure app.

discovery_confirm.title: Zendure set found
discovery_confirm.description: {model} with {packs} packs ({capacity} kWh), serial number {serial}, at {host}. Add it to ZEPHYR?

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the set or its answer is not usable. Check the address; if it still fails, turn HEMS on once in the Zendure app, leave the menu and turn it off again.

abort.already_configured: This set is already part of ZEPHYR.
abort.set_added: Set {number} has been added to ZEPHYR.
abort.cannot_connect: The set could not be reached.

data_description.host: IP address or host name of the Zendure set. HEMS must be off in the Zendure app.

reconfigure.title: Capacity of the set
reconfigure.description: ZEPHYR recognises most Zendure batteries by itself. Only enter the total capacity of this set when a pack is not recognised. 0 = automatic.

data_description.capacity_override: Total capacity of all batteries of this set together, in kWh. 0 = automatic from the pack table.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the set or its answer is not usable. Check the address; if it still fails, turn HEMS on once in the Zendure app, leave the menu and turn it off again.

abort.already_configured: This set is already part of ZEPHYR.

serial_mismatch.title: Different set at the address of set {number}
serial_mismatch.description: The device at {host} reports a different serial number than set {number}. ZEPHYR does not use it. Check the IP address of the set (for example a fixed address in your router), or remove set {number} and add it again.

unknown_pack.title: Battery of set {number} not recognised
unknown_pack.description: ZEPHYR does not recognise these batteries: {packs}. The capacity of set {number} is therefore too low. Enter the total capacity via ZEPHYR → Set {number} → Reconfigure. Want to help? Report the model and the line above in a GitHub issue, and we will add the battery.

p1_missing.title: No P1 meter chosen
p1_missing.description: ZEPHYR needs your smart meter to calculate. Open Settings → Devices & services → ZEPHYR → Configure and choose the P1 sensor (or the import and export sensors).

live_off_after_restart.title: ZEPHYR no longer controls the battery
live_off_after_restart.description: After a restart live control is off (option "Live control off after a restart"). The set keeps its last power until your current control or you take over. Switch "ZEPHYR controls the battery" on again, or let your current control take over.

second_controller.title: Another system controls the battery
second_controller.description: The set twice reported limits within 5 minutes that ZEPHYR did not write. ZEPHYR stopped writing and is back in shadow mode. Switch off your old control (Gielz, automations, the Zendure app) and then switch "ZEPHYR controls the battery" on again.

init.title: Sources and battery
init.description: Choose your smart meter (P1) in W: one net sensor (+ when drawing from the grid), or two sensors for import and export (as the DSMR integration provides). ZEPHYR runs in shadow mode: it calculates what it would do, but does not control the battery yet.

data.live_off_after_restart: Live control off after a restart (test phase)
data.expensive_hours: Deliver in the most expensive hours

data_description.p1_entity: A meter that reports every second controls best. With corrections (EV, air conditioning) you can choose the corrected sensor of your current setup.
data_description.min_soc: Below this value ZEPHYR stops delivering. Written to the set once ZEPHYR controls it.
data_description.max_soc: Above this value ZEPHYR stops charging. Written to the set once ZEPHYR controls it.
data_description.p1_source: Two sensors see every meter telegram, also when the value stays the same. Better than a combined template sensor, which only reports changes.
data_description.p1_import_entity: Power drawn from the grid, for example …_power_consumption.
data_description.p1_export_entity: Power returned to the grid, for example …_power_production.
data_description.solar_forecast_entity: Optional. A forecast sensor with half-hour detail (Solcast: …_forecast_tomorrow). ZEPHYR stores tomorrow's forecast every evening at 23:00, as a yardstick for the planner later.
data_description.solar_energy_entity: Optional. Total solar production in kWh (for example the inverter's energy counter). Read every hour to compare with the forecast.
data_description.live_off_after_restart: After a restart of Home Assistant or a reload, "ZEPHYR controls the battery" is off and you switch it on yourself. Keep this on during the test week.
data_description.price_entity: Optional. With a Nord Pool sensor (today's prices in its attributes) zero-meter control delivers only in the most expensive hours of the day. Without it ZEPHYR delivers whenever the house asks.
data_description.expensive_hours: Hours per day in which ZEPHYR may deliver: the most expensive according to Nord Pool.
data_description.reserve_soc: Extra charge that may be used freely: below it ZEPHYR charges in the cheapest hours before the next expensive block. In the expensive hours it delivers down to the minimum SOC. 0 = off.
data_description.min_price: Optional, bare Nord Pool price: never deliver below it, not even in the most expensive hours.

error.p1_pair_incomplete: Choose both the import and the export sensor.
error.p1_pair_same: Import and export must be two different sensors.

live_not_possible.message: ZEPHYR cannot control the battery now: {reasons}.

test_live.message: The write test only works in shadow mode ("ZEPHYR controls the battery" off).

test_not_standby.message: Set ZEPHYR to the mode Standby first for the write test.

test_command.name: Write test
test_command.description: Sends one fixed command to the set(s) and puts them back in standby after the chosen duration. Only in shadow mode with the mode Standby.
